newsitem.title: UK: SOFTS OUTLOOK - MARKETS EXPECTED QUIET, U.S. TO LEAD.
newsitem.headline: SOFTS OUTLOOK - MARKETS EXPECTED QUIET, U.S. TO LEAD.

text.p: London's soft commodity markets should stay seasonally quiet this week but will remain vulnerable to a shift of sentiment in New York or fresh fundamental news, traders said on Monday.

In robusta coffee the nearby Sept/Nov spread would probably draw most interest in London as the market moved independently of New York arabicas, which had recently rallied on perceived supply tightness.
The spread fluctuated between premium and discount throughout most of last week.
While LIFFE's revised grading criteria had caused an increase in robusta supply for the September position, ungraded coffees were still being hedged in the futures market, they said.
"Even though there have been grading problems over the last couple of months, people are aware there are plenty of robustas around," said one.
The discount was capable of widening to $16 but was still likely to give way to a premium, he added.

But other market sources said reduced buying interest due to a seasonal fall in demand might weaken nearby support for September, even though limited trade buying under current prices should be supportive.
"We're coming out of the summer period and the main robusta buyers are in the northern hemisphere," said one.
"There's no major rush to buy as (European) people are covered into September and October."
But more liquidity was needed further forward to encourage higher volume from nearby October which could be rolled.
London's white sugar market was finely balanced between a fundamentally bullish scenario, based on the usual perception of supply tightness in August, and a build-up of fund long positions.
The three or four funds still long in October whites were likely to sell if daily market closes continued at current levels -- leading to the bubble of strength bursting at some stage, they said.
Since the fund-led buying spree drove October to a new life-high of $331 at the end of July, the spot month had been drifting lower in generally light daily volumes.

"I think quite a lot of people were hoping more (sell) stops were going to be taken out," said one. But although October support looked reasonably solid, prices could still edge back to $321 or $320, he added.
Another trader was more sceptical of the degree of perceived weakness in the market, noting that $323 support was still relatively solid.
"I don't foresee it coming down with great speed," he said.
The October/October differential against New York was likely to attract trade buying as it was considered cheap at around $65, traders said.
Cocoa was expected to be the quietest of London's soft commodity markets, with little fundamental news likely until fresh crop information emerged, particularly from Ivory Coast and Ghana.
"All we hear is encouraging news out of Africa," said one trader. "There will be no fundamental news in the near future, the market's going to be sensitive to crop news."
On Friday London traders noted sentiment that the long liquidation seen recently in New York had played itself out.
"People feel that maybe New York has done its major move," said another trader.
